rationale: This Adobe-C++ functionobjects benchmark is dominated by compute-dense templated kernels (__introsort_loop, inner_product, accumulate) invoked under a timing harness, so runtime overhead must be capped while static analysis resistance stays high; SUB and IBR get the highest security/diversity weights because instruction substitution and indirect-branch conversion cheaply break pattern-matching and CFG recovery across the many small template-instantiated functions, while their low runtime profiles suit hot loops. SPLIT and IGV are weighted toward diversity at low cost, compounding per-function divergence across the 25 mostly-small functions without measurable slowdown. BCF is kept but with elevated RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so bogus control flow concentrates only on low-frequency functions (dispatch/setup in main) rather than the sort and accumulation inner loops. FLA's flattening carries the worst size and runtime tradeoffs for already-branch-heavy sorting code, so it is weighted mainly for diversity on mid-size non-kernel functions and suppressed where costs dominate. ICALL receives moderate weights: it converts direct calls to indirect ones for static-call-graph obfuscation, which is safe on this C++ source but adds indirect-branch cost in loops, hence the moderate RuntimeCost and a guarded CorrectnessRisk weight reflecting ABI/vtable sensitivity. All CorrectnessRisk weights are kept low-to-moderate so risk signals filter applications without disabling passes outright, preserving correctness on the small, well-typed codebase.
